invalid.because: `primitive` names something else, so a consumer dispatching on the property would upgrade the wrong node
`primitive` is missing altogether
the class string is missing the `qe-dv-data-table` token, so no renderer selector matches it
the class tokens are in the wrong order and double-spaced, which is not what the directive's normalisation produces
`tone` is outside the closed vocabulary neutral | accent | good | warn | bad
a `number` cell carries its value as a string, so a consumer cannot sort or scale it
a cell property is misspelled (`strongly` for `strong`); cell objects are closed so a typo cannot pass as data
a `bar` column is declared without the `max` it is drawn against
`decimals` is set on a `code` column, where there is no number to format
the table declares itself re-sortable but records no `sort` state, so the server-rendered order is unrecoverable
a `code` column is marked sortable; only number, bar and fraction columns may be in contract 1.0
a fallback `tableCell` has no children — the empty-cell failure the contract exists to prevent
`contract` is the number 1.0 rather than the string "1.0", so a version comparison would coerce and sort 1.10 below 1.9
the fallback is a `grid` rather than a `table`: `myst-to-tex` has no handler for grid and would drop the whole subtree while the build still exits 0
`children` is empty — a primitive whose fallback renders nothing does not implement this contract
`sort.order` is spelt out; the closed set is `asc` | `desc`
`nulls` is `first`, which contract 1.0 does not emit; the design's comparator puts nulls last in both directions
the class string repeats the family token `qe-dv` as an author token; the directive drops a token already present, so a repeat is a defect rather than a harmless duplicate

a body row carries a header cell: `myst-to-tex` writes a `\hline` after every row whose first cell is a header, so the table is ruled after every line, and its long-table path counts leading header rows away and emits a repeating running header with no body at all
the fallback table has no header row, so a reader of the plain build gets no column vocabulary and no consumer can tell the labels from the data
an inner `tableCell` describes itself with `contract` and `primitive`; only the root node carries those, and an inner node carries presentation and content only
the fallback cell repeats the cell object it renders, so the datum lives three times instead of twice and the copies can drift apart

the root carries a top-level `label`; `myst-cli`'s embed transform deletes `label`, `identifier` and `html_id` from every node that is not a crossReference, cite, footnote node, captionNumber or link, so the property works locally and silently disappears once the page is embedded elsewhere

a fallback cell holds a `card` node; `myst-to-tex` has no handler for `card` or `grid` and drops the whole subtree from the `.tex` while the build still exits 0, so the family closes a cell's inline content to `text`, `strong`, `emphasis`, `inlineCode` and `link`

the retired `naLabel` is carried on the root: the draft let each block spell a missing value for itself, contract 1.0 spells it one way — `null` in the properties, an em dash in the fallback — so a node still carrying the option sends a consumer looking for a string that means nothing
